transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-28 15:00 UTC — Duration: ~53 minutes. Recorded by Fireflies.
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Riley (Redwood SE), Sana Patel (Redwood SE), Jonas Park (Redwood CSM), Erin Walsh (Bridgeport Head of ML), Marcus Vega (Platform), Priya Shah (Security), Tommy Lin (Product)

Summary: quick demo of Redwood API + Console Optimize suggestions focused on migrating three vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Together) to a single Redwood onramp. Primary ask: parity with prompt/response behaviour, validation of latency/cost, and security posture for regulated PII workloads.
Topics: parity mapping, console routing policies, KV cache behavior, quantization tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private options, pilot scope, security requirements (KMS, SSO, audit logs)

00:00 Erin: okay thanks everyone for jumping on, we are eager to see how Redwood can take our current mix of providers down to one stack, trying to reduce vendor lock and cost.
00:12 Maya: great, thanks Erin. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE, and Liam and Sana from SE will run the parity mapping and console walkthrough. We'll start with a short checklist: endpoints you use, traffic shape, constraints like data residency and encryption at rest.
00:28 Marcus: most calls are OpenAI for general chat, Anthropic for some safety filtered flows, and Together for longform summarization. We have per-endpoint token budgets and different timeouts.
00:40 Liam: perfect, that's the typical hybrid stack. First slide is a mapping approach — map models to Redwood equivalents, align sampling/top-p/temp, and check prompt templates. We'll also demo the console where routing and fallbacks live.
01:03 Tommy: quick question, when you say "Redwood equivalents" what is the fidelity on completions — not just token counts but hallucination and style?
01:15 Sana: good call — parity is both syntactic and semantic. We do automated evals on sample prompts (BLEU/ROUGE-ish plus human checks) and runaway regression alerts. For style, we can tune system prompts and sampling to match the vendor's output distribution.
01:36 Priya: security — we need KMS integration and per-tenant key control, and SOC 2 evidence. Also audit logs for all requests and redaction.
01:47 Maya: yes — we'll share SOC2, ISO, and our KMS integration guide. You can deploy Redwood Private or Dedicated if you need customer-managed keys in a VPC. Audit logs available via Console -> Observability.

05:00 [screen share switches to Console]
05:12 Liam: here's the Console, per-route model assignments. You can see a rule here: route by path /summarize to a quantized Together-like checkpoint with more context length. Route /chat to our mid-size chat model. We also show a cost preview per token based on batching assumptions.
05:45 Marcus: that cost preview is nice — how do you compute batching benefits?
05:52 Liam: runtime monitors sequence length distribution and will suggest batch sizes — Optimize recommends batch=16 for your summarization workload given median seq len is 1,200 tokens. Batching reduces per-token GPU overhead but adds tail latency. We highlight expected p99 impact.
06:25 Marcus: p99 is our killer metric. Most of our SLAs are tied to 500ms p99 for interactive features.
06:32 Sana: right — for 500ms p99 we recommend Hosted for low throughput dev, or Dedicated with small pinned pool for production. For strict 500ms we also enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts which cuts token execution by skipping repeated prefix compute.
07:10 Erin: is KV cache compatible with the Together-style longform summarization? We often stream generations back.
07:18 Liam: yes, but streaming + KV caching has caveats: we keep KV open per session and it reduces latency on subsequent requests — but for single long streaming request there's less benefit. Also note we sometimes see people mispronounce "KV cash" in notes — sorry the transcriber does that.

08:40 Sana: switching to parity mapping example — here's a 3-way mapping table: OpenAI gpt-like -> Redwood-chat-medium, Anthropic Claude-like -> Redwood-safety-tuned, Together long -> Redwood-longform-quant. For each mapping we list sampling params, expected token delta, and a sample prompt/responses.
09:10 Marcus: show us the sample side-by-side.
09:18 Liam: sure. Example prompt A (customer support) — OpenAI response has shorter, more direct replies; Anthropic has cautious framing; Together longer. We adjust temperature from 0.2 to 0.35 for Redwood-chat-medium to emulate the shorter style. We add a safety instruction for the Claude-like mapping.
09:55 Erin: any automated diff tooling? We will need to measure hallucination rates across thousands of prompts.
10:02 Sana: yes — our Optimize suite runs prompt suites and computes regression metrics and can surface prompts with high semantic drift. We can import your test set and run head-to-head comparisons. That is typically used in the pilot.

12:20 Marcus: what about function/tool calling differences? We use structured tool calls with typed JSON currently with OpenAI functions.
12:30 Liam: Redwood supports function calling equivalents — you can register schemas in the Console and choose whether the model returns structured JSON or a textual summary. There are slight schema naming differences but we provide adapter config that maps your functions to Redwood's expected format.

15:00 [brief cross-talk; someone drops audio for 10s]
15:20 Priya: on compliance, do you retain raw logs? We need redaction at ingest for regulated PII.
15:30 Maya: retention is configurable per account. We offer automatic PII redaction rules and hashed-only audit logs when required. For Private deployment you can keep logs entirely in your VPC.

18:50 Liam: demo time — I'm going to run a live conversion: an OpenAI chat endpoint request mapped to Redwood via the adapter. I'll send the same prompt to both and show side-by-side output and token accounting.
19:05 [typing sounds]
19:20 Liam: sending now. OpenAI returned in 320ms, Redwood hosted equivalent returned in 360ms but with 12% lower token usage due to prefix caching and aggressive byte-pair token packing. The style is very similar — we tuned system prompt.
19:50 Marcus: 360ms p50 okay but p99 was 1.2s in your preview — that's above our target. Can that be improved?
20:05 Sana: yes, for p99 we can move to Dedicated with pinned GPUs. Also recommend turning on lower latency kernel selection (we auto-select kernels; for your L4 sequences we can force a low-latency path with slight cost increase).
20:28 Marcus: what's the cost delta for that?
20:35 Liam: in your case about +18% unit cost but p99 drops to ~520–560ms based on similar customers. We'll include modeled numbers in the parity spreadsheet.

24:00 Tommy: we also have multi-tenant data isolation concerns — can we restrict models per team and limit tokens?
24:12 Jonas: yes — Console has per-team quotas, RBAC roles, and route-level model pins. For Dedicated you'll also get network isolation and private endpoints.

27:30 Erin: curious about quantization artifacts. Our Together workloads benefit from int4 quantized checkpoints to fit the long sequences in memory — does Redwood support that?
27:42 Liam: we do. Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles per model and workload. We support int8 and experimental int4 paths; for longform we often recommend int8 with KV sharding to avoid accuracy regressions. We'll show example accuracy vs cost curves.

32:11 [screen shows Optimize recommendations page]
32:20 Sana: here are recommended profiles — you can simulate cost & latency impact and preview estimated quality delta. For your summarize workloads, we recommend QProfile-LONG-1 (int8 + 4k context optim) — gives roughly 35% cost reduction with <2% measured semantic regress.
33:05 Marcus: what's the basis for the <2% number? Is it human-annotated?
33:12 Sana: it's cohort evaluation on a mixture of your sample prompts and public benchmarks; we always do a manual spot-check in pilot before rolling.

36:00 Priya: encryption in transit — do you support customer-supplied TLS certs and private endpoints?
36:10 Maya: yes for Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports mTLS to private connectors; for strict handoff you can use VPC peering and customer-managed TLS termination.

39:40 Liam: technical deep dive — resource layout for a Dedicated pool. Each worker pins a model variant; autoscaler keeps spare slots for burst. We showed a small cluster config used by another finance customer — they pinned 4 GPUs and got predictable p99s.
40:20 Marcus: do you have a performance runbook? We need to reproduce results in our environment.
40:28 Liam: we'll share the runbook along with the parity spreadsheet — includes sequence length distribution capture, synthetic load generator, and exact sampling params.

44:00 Tommy: rollback & canary strategy? We run nightly rollouts.
44:10 Jonas: Console supports canary by percentage, header-based routing, and automatic fallback to previous model on error spikes. You can set automatic revert thresholds.

47:30 Erin: okay let's review pilot scope and timeline. We want a 2-week pilot: 3 endpoints, one low-latency chat, one safety-sensitive flow, and one longform summarizer. We'll evaluate based on p99 latency, token cost delta, and semantic parity score.
47:50 Maya: sounds good. Proposed: week 1 ingest & mapping, week 2 benchmark + manual checks. We'll need traces and a shared test set.
48:10 Erin: yes we can provide traces and up to 5,000 historical prompts for evaluation.
48:22 Maya: perfect — action items noted. Liam will share the parity mapping and console screenshots. Maya will send security docs and licensing notes. Jonas will coordinate pilot schedule.

51:00 Marcus: small nit — any known incompatibilities with your adapter and our typed function names? We use snake_case heavily.
51:10 Liam: adapter will map snake_case to the expected schema; we log schema mismatches and can auto-generate transformation hooks.

52:00 Maya: recap and next steps: we'll send the spreadsheet and security pack; customer uploads traces; schedule pilot for week of Jan 10. Any final questions?
52:12 Erin: no, thanks all. This was helpful.
52:18 Maya: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links in the next 48 hours.
52:25 [meeting ends]

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors (names, acronyms). Shared artifacts mentioned: parity_mapping_v1.xlsx (link to be shared), redwood-security-pack.pdf, pilot-runbook.md.
